Load functions and packages

Load the packages and other functions that will be used during reorganisation.

source('HS_functions.R')

Load data

Load the raw data

Load the raw data exported from Excel to csv.

path_file = "0Data/hs_dance_reorg.csv"
if(!file.exists(path_file))
{print(path_file, '\nnot found')}
hd = read.table(file = path_file, 
                header = T, 
                sep  = ',')

Inspect data

Check the names of variables in this dataset.

names(hd)

Format data

Ensure that each variable has the correct data format for subsequent analysis.

hd = within(hd, {
  ID = as.factor(ID) # bee identifier as a factor
  ID_d = as.factor(ID_d) # beedance identifier as a factor
  day = as.factor(day) # date as a factor
  condition = factor(
    condition,
    levels = c(
      "vertical",
      "horizontal",
      "tilted",
      "solar",
      "antisolar",
      "zenith"
    )
  ) #set up conditions as a factor in preferred order
  sast_time = as.POSIXct(
    sast_time,
    tz = "Africa/Johannesburg",
    format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS"
  ) #South African Standard time
  cangle = circular(
    feeder_angle,
    template = 'none'
  ) #circular formatted angle for circular functions
})

u_id = with(hd, unique(ID)) #unique dancers
length(u_id)#40 bees
## [1] 40
u_id_d = with(hd, unique(ID_d)) # unique beedances
length(u_id_d)#377 beedances
## [1] 408

Plot Examples

Set up plot parameters

In each plot, we will indicate the condition and time of day using different colours. Experiment times will be added for reference (in seconds after midnight).

#condition colours
cond_cols = list(
  vertical = 'darkred',
  horizontal = 'darkgreen',
  tilted = 'seagreen',
  solar = 'blue4',
  antisolar = 'cyan4',
  zenith = "skyblue3"
)


#assign experiment times
morning_start = 7.50 * 60 * 60
morning_end = 9.00 * 60 * 60
midday_start = 11.00 * 60 * 60
midday_end = 13.00 * 60 * 60
afternoon_start = 15.00 * 60 * 60
afternoon_end = 16.50 * 60 * 60
evening_start = 17.50 * 60 * 60
evening_end = 19.00 * 60 * 60

exper_times = c(
  morning_start = morning_start,
  morning_end = morning_end,
  midday_start = midday_start,
  midday_end = midday_end,
  afternoon_start = afternoon_start,
  afternoon_end = afternoon_end,
  evening_start = evening_start,
  evening_end = evening_end
)


time_cols = c(
  morning_start   = "#C68B59",
  morning_end     = "#C68B59",
  midday_start    = "#E6C594",
  midday_end      = "#E6C594",
  afternoon_start = "#C68B59",
  afternoon_end   = "#C68B59",
  evening_start   = "#94B49F",
  evening_end     = "#94B49F"
)

Plot an example dance

For example we can look at the dances for Blue-22 recorded on 2025-01-28 at 08:12, 08:36, 08:58, 08:34 & 11:44—each of which is the first for one of the conditions. Dances are plotted relative to sun position (0°) and feeder azimuth is shown as an brown line.

example_day  = unique(hd$day)[length(unique(hd$day))]#last day
example_bee = "22b"
print(paste("First dance for", example_bee, "for each condition on", example_day))
## [1] "First dance for 22b for each condition on 20250128"
daybee_lst = FirstDanceCond(dta = hd,
                        subset = day %in% example_day & ID %in% example_bee)  
## [1] "First dance for each condition after subsetting"
##            [,1]                                       
## vertical   "22b_00002_08:12:00_20250128"              
## horizontal "22b_00012_08:36:00_20250128"              
## antisolar  "22b_2025-01-28 07-57-05_08:58:00_20250128"
## solar      "22b_2025-01-28 10-44-09_11:44:00_20250128"
## zenith     NA                                         
## tilted     "22b_00010_08:29:00_20250128"
# Plot the example subset
Plt_subs(subs = daybee_lst$example_subs,
         angle_for = "sun",
         cond_cols = cond_cols,
         title = paste("First dance for", example_bee, "for each condition on", example_day)
         )

At least for this subset, the dances follow the expected pattern. For both vertical and horizontal dances, the average waggle run aligns with the feeder direction. With antisolar skylight the waggle runs are also aligned, while solar skylight is mistaken for antisolar skylight, resulting in a 180° turn.

We can also plot these dances with the feeder direction subtracted, so that the feeder falls at 0°.

#Plot using the feeder as the frame of reference
Plt_subs(subs = daybee_lst$example_subs,
         angle_for = "feeder",
         title = paste("Feeder angles for 1st dance of", example_bee, "for each condition on", example_day))

Solar Ephemeris

Using the vertical dances, it should be possible to identify the solar ephemeris functions used by those individuals that danced repeatedly throughout the day.

Check dance times

Blue 22 and blue 66 both danced very frequently, so we can start by checking when they danced.

par(mfrow = c(1,1))
#plot all vertical dances
with(subset(hd, condition %in% c("vertical") ),
     {
     plot(x = GetToD(sast_time,
                     tz = 'UTC'),
          y = Mod360.180(sun_az),
          xlim = c(20400,78060),#"06:40:00 CET" "22:41:00 CET"
          ylim = c(-1,1)*180,
          xlab = 'UTC',
          ylab = 'Sun Azimuth',
          main = 'Vertical dances',
          pch = 3,#cross
          col = 'gray50'
     )
     abline(h = -4:4*c(45),
            lty = 2) #limits
     abline(v =  12*60*60, #as.numeric(as.POSIXct("1970-01-01 12:00:00 UTC"))
            lty = 3)
     }
)
#add lines indicating the approximate expected start and end of each experiment
abline(v = exper_times,
       col = time_cols,
       lty = c(1,2),
       lwd = 2
       )

              ID %in% c('22b', '66b')

It looks like we have the best chance with blue 22, for which we have the most dances during the rapid azimuth change period in the middle of the day.

  x = 'bottomright',

  pch = c(3, 19),

It looks like B22 is fairly representative: all bees are initially slow to adjust to the sun’s accelerating westward movement after 11:00, but have adjusted by 12:00. In the afternoon dances start at the correct angle, appear not to adjust at all during the following hour, but begin to adjust around 17:30. A simple description could be achieved with a piecewise regression, with a constant rate of change in solar azimuth between 07:00 and 11:00, another (faster) rate of change between 11:00 and 13:00, and likely the same morning rate of change repeated again between 13:00 and 19:00.

Calculate dance means

#calculate mean vectors
mean_vectors = aggregate(cangle~ID_d+ #for each dance 
                           ID+condition+sun_az+sun_el + # also save these variables
                           time+day,
                         data = hd,
                         FUN = rho.circular
)
#correct names
mean_vectors = within(mean_vectors,
                      {mean_vector = cangle; rm(cangle)} # angle now indicates a mean vector, not an angle
)
#add kappa
mle_estimates = aggregate(cangle~ID_d+ #for each dance 
                           ID+condition+sun_az+sun_el + # also save these variables
                           time+day,
                          data = hd,
                          FUN = MLE_est
)
#Rayleigh tests
rayleigh_tests = aggregate(cangle~ID_d+ #for each dance 
                           ID+condition+sun_az+sun_el + # also save these variables
                           time+day,
                          data = hd,
                          FUN = Rayleigh_p
                          )

#correct names
rayleigh_tests = within(rayleigh_tests,
                      {p_rayleigh = cangle; rm(cangle)} # angle now indicates a mean vector, not an angle
)

#add to the summary table and 
#calculate inverse softplus kappa
mean_vectors = within(mean_vectors,
                      {
                        mu = deg(mle_estimates$cangle[,'mu'])
                        kappa = mle_estimates$cangle[,'kappa']
                      }
)
#check how many dances would count as "oriented"
print(paste("Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of all dances:") )
## [1] "Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of all dances:"
#all dances
with(rayleigh_tests,
     print( mean(p_rayleigh <0.05) *100,digits = 2)
     )
## [1] 77
#by condition
for(cond in levels(rayleigh_tests$condition))
{
  
print(paste("Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of", cond, "dances:") )
with(subset(rayleigh_tests,
            subset = condition %in% cond),
     print(mean(p_rayleigh <0.05) *100,digits = 2)
     )
}
## [1] "Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of vertical dances:"
## [1] 91
## [1] "Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of horizontal dances:"
## [1] 66
## [1] "Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of tilted dances:"
## [1] 94
## [1] "Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of solar dances:"
## [1] 74
## [1] "Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of antisolar dances:"
## [1] 66
## [1] "Rayleigh p<0.05, proportion of zenith dances:"
## [1] 60
par(mar = c(3, 3, 0, 0))
boxplot(mean_vector~condition,
        data = mean_vectors,
        ylim = c(0,1),
        col = adjustcolor(cond_cols, alpha.f = 0.1),
        border = 'gray50',
        outline = FALSE)
stripchart(mean_vector~condition,
           data = mean_vectors,
           add = TRUE,
           vertical = TRUE,
           method = 'jitter',
           col = adjustcolor(cond_cols, alpha.f = 0.5),
           bg = gray(level = 0,
                     alpha = 0.1),
           pch = 21)
#Identify stimuli
abline(h = c(0,1))

mv_agg =  aggregate(mean_vector~condition,
           data = mean_vectors,
           FUN = quantile,
           probs = c(0.5, 0.25, 0.75))
rownames(mv_agg) = with(hd, levels(condition))
mv_agg = within(mv_agg, rm(condition))
mv_agg = t(apply(mv_agg, MARGIN = 1, unlist))
print(mv_agg,
  digits = 3)

## antisolar            0.644           0.504           0.876
## zenith               0.738           0.616           0.785
par(mfrow = c(2,3), 
    mar = c(0,0,0,0),
    oma = c(2,0,0,0))
for(cond in levels(hd$condition))
{
PCfun(angles = subset(mean_vectors, 
                      subset = condition %in% cond)$mu,
      col = cond_cols[[cond]],
      shrink = 2.8,
      title = cond)
}
mtext(text = "mean dance angles relative to feeder",
      side = 1,
      line = 0.2,
      outer = TRUE)

for(tod in c('sun_el < 15', 
             'sun_el < 45 & sun_el > 30',
             'sun_el > 75'
             )
    )
{
  
  # tod_filter = eval(str2lang(tod), envir = mean_vectors)
  for(cond in levels(hd$condition))
{
    cond_tod_mu = subset(mean_vectors, 
                      subset = condition %in% cond &
                        eval(str2lang(tod))

    if(length(cond_tod_mu)>0)

        xlab = "",
        ylab = "",

      )
      legend(x = "center",
             legend = paste("no", cond, "data found"))
    }
}

      side = 1,
